2_Introduction: The device achieved a remarkable PCE of 20.2947%, with a VOC of 1.1106 V, JSC of 23.592 mA/cm², and FF of 77.453%. The perovskite (Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2) solution was prepared with a concentration of 1.5 mol/L in mixed solvent of DMF and DMSO. The precursor solution was spin-coated onto the substrate surface at 1000 rpm for 10 s, then accelerated to 4700 rpm for 35 s. During the second spin coating step, 200 µL of CB was deposited onto the perovskite film 8 seconds before the program ended. Then the films were annealed at 115 °C for 30 min to form the perovskite layer.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂—featuring a carefully tuned A-site cation distribution that enhances phase stability and suppresses δ-phase formation while maintaining a near-ideal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and mitigating halide segregation and Pb²⁺-mediated ion migration—is precisely governed by the kinetic interplay between precursor concentration (1.5 mol/L), solvent coordination strength (DMF:DMSO mixture promoting intermediate adduct formation), spin-coating dynamics (initial low-speed wetting followed by high-shear dewetting at 4700 rpm), and antisolvent intervention (200 µL chlorobenzene delivered at the critical 8 s mark to trigger instantaneous nucleation without premature aggregation). This temporally resolved crystallization protocol yields highly uniform, pinhole-free films with large, oriented grains and minimal residual PbI₂—as corroborated by XRD showing complete suppression of the characteristic 12.6° PbI₂ peak and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection—while optical and PL mapping reveal spatially homogeneous film coverage (>99.2% continuity), negligible grayscale intensity fluctuations (<3% RSD), and uniformly elevated photoluminescence intensity with monoexponential decay kinetics (τ₁ = 382 ns), collectively indicating suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways across the entire active area. The resulting structural integrity, morphological homogeneity, and low defect density synergistically enable efficient charge extraction and minimal interfacial recombination, culminating in a VOC of 1.1106 V, JSC of 23.592 mA/cm², FF of 77.453%, and PCE of 20.2947%.
